 Wyoming - For his final budget, Governor Mark Gordan is proposing a $527 million budget to account for ongoing expenses as well as pad for anything that may come up.
 Wyoming's supplemental budget is a financial plan created every other year for the General Session.
 Governor Gordan says, "I think a budget statement is kind of about the things we care about." 
 Included in his supplemental budget is property tax relief.
 The Governor proposed the continuation of refunds for eligible homeowners.
 "We wanted to make sure, considering property taxes is still a very important issue," Gordan explains, "that we put 15.56 million to fully fund existing property tax refund programs." 
 SUN bucks, an existing summer food assistance program, helped 37,000 Wyoming children las summer.
 Gordan recommends approximately $436,000 in one-time funding to prepare the program for the 2027 year.
 Additionally, he recommended $575,000 in ongoing funding for the state's share of the administration going forward.
 "It's important to continue this program. It's something that I have heard repeatedly over the course of this year how important that program was to make sure kids were not dealing with hunger," he says.
 Other proposed funding included $30 million for the prevention and control for wildfires and invasive species, a $100 million addition to Wyoming's savings, $500,000 in legal defense funds to protect Wyoming's water, export, and industry interest, and funds that meet existing public education funding obligations.
 "...of critical concern that the people of Wyoming know that these funds have been carefully shepherded and managed," says Gordan.
 The purpose of the supplemental budget is to address unexpected needs, revenue shortfalls, or new programs that have arisen since the core biennial budget was passed.
 The supplemental budget plan will go through legislature during next year's 68th session.
 You can find the full supplemental budget on the State Budget Office's website.
